title: State-triggered cooperative mandatory merging at temporary lane closures in mixed traffic flow
content:
by Jie Yu, Tao Chen, Qiang Wen, Mingyuan Bai

Cooperation can create space at a temporary lane closure, but unnecessary intervention can increase traffic disturbance and fuel use. We develop ECO, a state-triggered strategy that links selective gap creation to mandatory merge execution. Initial target-lane density, remaining distance and controllable-neighbor availability govern activation. Longitudinal model predictive control shapes the gap, while predictive admission, lateral tracking and bounded safety filtering govern execution. Paired simulations assume that all vehicles, including those with nominal human-driving behavior, permit final safety intervention. Across 20 conditions with nonzero target-lane connected and automated vehicle penetration, ECO reduces fuel intensity by 0.80%–7.20% relative to the specified continuous-cooperation controller and completes all 500 main runs. With identical controller settings, activation gating reduces fuel intensity by 1.22%–5.37% at low density and has no effect at the tested higher densities. In a 57-vehicle queue, ECO completes 88.33% of merges versus 66.67% for passive merging, at slightly higher full-horizon fuel use and delay. These results identify a conditional service benefit of cooperation and distinguish it from the operating savings obtained by suppressing unnecessary gap creation.
